plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant, five-petaled blossoms on bare branches in late winter, often while snow is still on the ground. It is widely cultivated in Japan, China, and Korea, and the fruit is used for pickles (umeboshi) and liqueur.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (late January to March)
plants.location: East Asia (Japan, China, Korea); cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are celebrated in East Asia as symbols of perseverance and hope because they bloom in the cold, before cherry blossoms.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: Australia's national floral emblem, a small tree or large shrub with fluffy, golden, ball-shaped flower clusters and sickle-shaped phyllodes. It is a key nectar and pollen source for native insects and birds.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere (typically July to October, with some early blooms and related wattles flowering in summer)
plants.location: Southeastern Australia (Victoria, South Australia, New South Wales)
plants.funFact: Australia celebrates National Wattle Day on September 1, and the golden and green of the wattle are the country's official national colors.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with drooping, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. Snowdrops often push through frost and snow, naturalizing in woodlands and gardens across Europe.
plants.location: Europe, from the Pyrenees to Ukraine; naturalized in the UK and North America
plants.funFact: Snowdrops contain galantamine, a compound that has been developed into a medication used to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub with large flower heads up to 30 cm across, made of pink or cream bracts surrounding a central cluster of tiny florets. It is adapted to nutrient-poor soils and fire-prone fynbos habitat.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly spring and summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowering spanning much of the year in some populations, including late summer
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape, South Africa; cultivated in Australia, California, and Hawaii
plants.funFact: The king protea is the national flower of South Africa, and the genus Protea is named after the Greek god Proteus, who could change his shape.
